verdict.reasoning: Patient states dizziness with room spinning started about two hours ago and has been continuous: "Started probably about two hours ago maybe" and "Yeah it's, it's there, the whole time" and doctor confirms "So it's there now for the past two hours you'd say, yeah?"
Patient describes onset while making breakfast and associated symptoms: "I was just actually making my husband some breakfast" and "I just suddenly felt very fuzzy and dizzy, um, and a bit shaky."

Patient reports unsteady gait: "I can't, I can't walk properly. Uh, well I can walk properly but not straight" and attributes it to room moving: "I don't feel like I'm stable. My, the room is spinning."
Ear buzzing with preserved hearing is described: "my ears are buzzing a bit" and later "It's just a bit of a buzzy noise in my ears, but otherwise I can hear everything."
Patient denies vomiting but reports nausea: "Have you been physically sick?" "No, but now I'm feeling very sick." Doctor labels it as nausea: "Nausea, OK."
Patient denies recent viral illness and temperature: "Did you have any kind of viral illness in the recent past..." "No." and later "Do you have a temperature at all?" "I don't think so."

No limb weakness or focal deficit: patient says "My, my legs and arms and everything are working fine" and doctor repeats "So there's no weakness of your arms and legs. OK." with patient answering "No."
Past similar episode timing and duration: "I had a a similar sort of thing about a month ago" and when asked duration: "Probably only about five, ten minutes."
Past medical history: "I've had premature ovarian failure"
Current medication: same sentence indicates HRT use: "I've had premature ovarian failure, um, and I've taken HRT."
Allergy status: doctor asks "do you have any allergies at all?" and patient replies "No."

Doctor explicitly suspects labyrinthitis and the reasoning elements match the history: "the most common... diagnosis we would you're suffering from at the moment is something called labyrinthitis" after hearing about acute continuous vertigo, ear buzzing, nausea, unsteady gait, and the absence of hearing loss, fever, recent viral illness, or limb weakness.

Combination statement summarizes prior facts: patient reports "premature ovarian failure" and "I've taken HRT," supporting that she has premature ovarian failure and is on hormone replacement therapy.

Prescription details: "It's called , yeah? It's one tablet three times a day. So I'll give you about ten days worth" and later "It doesn't really matter, you can take it... might as well just take the tablets," indicating it need not be taken with food. Drug name is inaudible/not stated.

In-person review plan: "I would still like you to be seen by one of our doctors to take a look inside your ears" and "while you're with the doctors, we'd like to do your blood pressure, just examine your, you know, you know, how your walking and everything is" and "In the interim, obviously in the next few days, you'll get to see one of my doctors".

Safety-net advice: "if you double up any weakness of your legs or arms or, or, you know, a sudden headache... or you start being violently sick with it, then you know, you would need to take your to A and E." This includes new limb weakness, sudden severe headache, and violent vomiting.
Appointment booking advice: "Just make sure you call support to book that appointment, OK?"
